A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneDC, with matching authors, architecture, objectives, and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression evaluations, semantic-guidance and loss ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative reconstructions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original OneDC evaluations and adds results including bitrate-allocation ablations, memory measurements, and expanded benchmark comparisons.

M1.justification: The latent codec, FSQ hyperprior, semantic distillation, one-step generator, LoRA adaptation, and two-stage objectives remain unchanged. The explicit cross-attention equation and revised diagrams explain existing operations; expanded rate settings do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training source and evaluate natural-image compression on Kodak, CLIC2020, MS-COCO 30K, and DIV2K, with COCO2017 semantic-reconstruction examples. DIV2K and cropped CLIC2020 already appear in v1's appendix. Added resizing and cropping configurations change protocols rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds DDCM comparisons using published scores and separately compares against original PerCo results (Figures 8 and 10). Renaming the existing reimplementation to PerCo (SD) is only clarification. DiffC also disappears from the retained cropped CLIC2020 comparison using 256-pixel FID patches (v1 Figure 9; v2 Figure 12), although it remains elsewhere.

E3.justification: Appendix B expands the rate-control settings from four lambda values to seven, adding 0.6, 1.0, and 12.2. New DDCM comparisons use resized and center-cropped Kodak 512 and CLIC2020 768 images, with respective FID patch sizes of 64 and 128. The earlier CLIC2020 protocol using 256-pixel patches is retained separately.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted bitrate-allocation ablation holding the hyperprior at 0.0035 bpp while varying latent bits, including zero latent bits (Table 4). Parameter-count and memory comparisons supplement the existing efficiency analysis. The original semantic-guidance and hybrid-loss ablations, including Table 1 values, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Revised FID patch protocols concern evaluation settings, without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 revises DiffC-relative LPIPS bitrate savings from 50.08% to 55.27% on Kodak and from 56.02% to 54.60% on CLIC2020; the MS-COCO PerCo FID saving changes from 42.94% to 39.55%. Table 2's baseline BD-Rates change substantially. Expanded operating points and new comparator, allocation, and memory results add substantial evidence. These revisions should not all be interpreted as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The new standard cross-attention equation spells out the conditioning operation already described in v1. Appendix B retains the same KL/score derivation and training losses; no substantive mathematical assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the headline bitrate-saving claim from over 40% to over 39%. The central contributions—one-step compression, distilled hyperprior guidance, hybrid-domain training, and over 20-fold decoding acceleration—retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the allocation results as evidence that hyperprior bits provide semantics while latent bits preserve detail. It discusses OneDC's higher memory consumption than DDCM and describes realism against DDCM as competitive, while restricting the blanket lower-FID comparison to full-resolution CLIC2020. Existing real-time and reconstruction-authenticity limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds cross-attention tensor details, separates the diffusion U-Net's base and LoRA parameter counts, and reports approximately six and twelve days for the two training stages. It provides more explicit crop/FID instructions and replaces the future code-release statement with a project URL. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware, and training-schedule details already existed.

R1.justification: Related work gains a conventional learned-compression subsection and references covering foundational compression, the distortion-perception tradeoff, diffusion foundations, consistency models, and DDCM. The Relic et al. discussion is removed. These broaden context without substantially redefining OneDC's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 expands related-work and conditioning explanations, revises evaluation prose, corrects figure references and grammar, and updates publication front matter. The main section sequence and most methodological, ablation, conclusion, and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework and training diagrams, reorganizes rate-distortion panels, brings additional metrics into the main comparison, and adds dedicated DDCM and original-PerCo plots. New Tables 3–10 present complexity, allocation, and numerical benchmark data. Existing qualitative figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for its comparative claims by supplementing the PerCo reimplementation with original-PerCo and DDCM comparisons under explicit protocols, while qualifying its realism advantage. Numerical tables improve auditability, and the allocation analysis and memory measurements better substantiate component roles and practical tradeoffs. These gains outweigh the narrower comparator coverage in one supplementary cropped comparison; the improvement comes from stronger evidence and clearer qualification, not higher reported scores.
